newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares ended lower after the index had been lingering at a depressed level all day on Thursday.
The AEX blue chip index closed 5.22 points lower at 733.47 and the AMX midcap index was also down 11.86 points at 1,133.38.
"Business was very thin and there were only very few buyers," said one dealer. He added that the undertone in the market was still good, particularly as the dollar was steady in afternoon trade.
Lower prices in the bond market had pressured financials, but dealers said there was still potential for those stocks.
Bank-insurer ING, seen as a good buy by dealers, was 0.10 guilders lower at 74.10.
Other financials were hit harder by the lower bond market. ABN AMRO fell 2.30 guilders to 124.80.
Insurer Stad Rotterdam was 1.90 guilders lower after it had earlier released almost 18 percent higher 1996 net profits at 156.9 million guilders.
The figures were in line with analysts' expectations.
Building firm NBM Amstelland closed 0.50 guilders lower at 44.40, after announcing that 1996 net had doubled and giving an upbeat forecast for earnings per share in 1997.
Smallcap Reesink fell sharply after announcing a 40 percent fall in first quarter 1997 profits, but the stock recovered a little near the close.
Reesink closed 7.80 guilders lower at 145.00, after hitting a day's low of 140.00.
